Summary: Canonical name resolution from the SEC listed-company file: exact and unique-prefix names resolve to a CIK and are verified by CIK; near matches are suggestions only; ambiguous names stay unresolved
Description: 1) Original intent: a selected subject resolves to one canonical identity (CIK) from a canonical name source, deterministically and with disclosure; an approximate or ambiguous name is never silently bound (Founder approval 2026-10-11 of specs/proposal-canonical-name-resolution-20261011.md with the correction that a unique prefix is only a candidate and must pass the existing CIK-based SEC verification). 2) Acceptance criteria: (a) exact legal-name match is eligible to bind, then verified by CIK; (b) a unique prefix of 4+ characters is a candidate only and binds only after the SEC annual-filings verification of that CIK succeeds; (c) a near match (edit distance, misspelt legal suffix tolerated) is a suggestion only, never bound, shown as 'Closest listed registrant: <NAME>, not assumed.' with no new control; (d) an ambiguous match stays unresolved with its candidates; (e) suffix tolerance affects suggestions only and never weakens verification; (f) engine route GET /api/sec-names with a daily server-side cache and a local vite proxy; the production nginx rule is specified and NOT applied; (g) cases: Ford Motor Company, Ford Motor Compnany, Ford, Frod, Fordd, Tesle, Meta, C07/C11 and registered subjects unchanged; (h) focused tests for exact, prefix, ambiguous and near behaviour; existing admission and subject suites green; no rescoring. 3) Current implementation state: proposal approved 2026-10-11; implementation starting. 4) Dependencies: KRYL-1380 (SEC filer admission), DEF-1406 (subject selection), KRYL-1398 (snapshot lookup). 5) Superseded by a newer ticket: no; extends KRYL-1380's verification rule. 6) Maps to the current product model: yes (subject first, identity by CIK, evidence-bound). Production exposure of /api/sec-names requires separate Founder approval.
